messages.author: d74687e854baa17e
messages.subject: Factor loading regression weights / Factor Scores Regressions - can they be obtained in lavaan?
parts:
Hello everyone,

I would love to be able to obtain factor loading regression weights from lavaan, but I haven't been able to figure out how

These are different to factor loadings, and are called "Factor Scores Regressions'" in Lisrel output

This reference ncac.acecqa.gov.au/reports/report-documents/composite_variables.pdf notes their calculation in footnote 7 on page 7 (attached as picture)

Also, the figure on page 8 has the factor loadings and Table 2 on page 9 has the corresponding regression weights (also attached as picture).

If anyone knows how to obtain factor loading regression weights in lavaan and is willing to share that would be great!

At the moment I am running most of my analysis in lavaan and then running a final version in Lisrel to obtain the regression weights, so a solution would really helpful

I am also using categorical data if that complicates things

Kind Regards,

Peter

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: Factor loading regression weights / Factor Scores Regressions - can they be obtained in lavaan?
parts:
On 02/07/2017 09:38 AM, Peter wrote:
> If anyone knows how to obtain factor loading regression weights in
> lavaan and is willing to share that would be great!

See ?lavPredict

library(lavaan)
example(cfa)
out <- lavPredict(fit, fsm = TRUE)
attr(out, "fsm")

Yves.

On 02/07/2017 12:48 PM, Peter wrote:
> Does that mean ordinal or categorical data will not report the fsm?

Yes. In the categorical/ordinal case, there is no factor-score
regression matrix. Factor scores are computed in a different way.

Yves.

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: Factor loading regression weights / Factor Scores Regressions-can they be obtained in lavaan?
parts:
On 06/30/2017 11:07 AM, Jorge Sinval wrote:
> I get this:
>
> Error in solve.default(VETAx[[g]]) :
> system is computationally singular: reciprocal condition number =
> 8.75384e-18

This means that the variance-(covariance) matrix of your latent
variables (eta) (hence, VETA) is not positive definite. You can check
this by typing:

lavInspect(fit, "cov.lv")
lavInspect(fit, "cor.lv") # correlation metric

If you have a negative variance, or a correlation higher than 1, then
there is no way to compute factor scores.

(the lesson for me is that lavPredict() should check this first, and
complain, instead of letting it fail)

Yves.

parts:
Error in solve.default(VETAx[[g]]) : 
  system is computationally singular: reciprocal condition number = 8.75384e-18

I think that is an issue with your data/model, not lavPredict().  It does work in general:

library(semTools)
model <- '
  f1 =~ u1 + u2 + u3 + u4
  f2 =~ u5 + u6 + u7 + u8
  f3 =~ 1*f1 + 1*f2
'
fit <- cfa(model, datCat)
head(lavPredict(fit))


             f1         f2          f3
[1,] -0.2786596 -0.4595026 -0.26319984
[2,] -0.4497644 -0.4270190 -0.31364747
[3,] -0.3131084  0.1710520 -0.05289115
[4,] -1.0141931 -0.5600881 -0.56495805
[5,]  0.6077838  0.8295970  0.51307266
[6,]  0.2951244 -0.1930175  0.03862851
